issues.detail: The Greek 'μη σχισωμεν αυτον' (let us not tear it) refers to the garment/robe. The Vietnamese 'Chớ xé áo nầy' implies 'this robe', but the Greek 'αυτον' is a pronoun referring back to the object of interest (the robe), and 'αλλα λαχωμεν περι αυτου' means 'but let us cast lots *about* it/concerning it'. The Vietnamese 'bắt thăm xem ai được' (cast lots to see who gets) loses the specific focus on the garment as the object of the lot-casting.
The Greek 'τινος εσται' (who shall be [the one]) is omitted in the Vietnamese translation of the first quote, which simplifies it to 'ai được'.
